title: Perfect tensor cohomology detects upper boundedness
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose that for every perfect object $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] there is an integer $b_P$ such that $H^i(R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}K))=0$ for all $i>b_P$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Then there is an integer $b$ such that $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all $i>b$. No uniform bound on the $b_P$ is required.

proof.text:
For every perfect $Q$ on $X$, its dual $Q^\vee$ is perfect and $R\mathcal Hom(Q,K)\cong K\otimes^LQ^\vee$ by the perfect RHom comparison. Derived tensor symmetry and the definition of global RHom give
$$H^i(R\Gamma(X,Q^\vee\otimes^LK))\cong H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],K).$$
The last comparison is the shifted-global-Hom equivalence with $f=\mathrm{id}_X$, $m=-i$, $n=0$. The tensor-test hypothesis applied to $Q^\vee$ therefore makes the right side zero for $i\gg0$, separately for each $Q$. We prove below that this all-perfect-Hom condition forces upper boundedness on any qcqs scheme.

For a qcqs scheme $T$, let $\mathscr P(T)$ mean: every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ for which $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],E)=0$ for $i\gg0$ for each perfect $Q$ is bounded above. Apply the qcqs-open induction principle to this property. For the affine base $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, take the perfect object $Q=\mathcal O_T[0]$. The K-injective definition gives $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_T[0],E)\cong E$: evaluation at $1$ identifies its Hom complex with the chosen injective representative. Thus the shifted-global-Hom equivalence identifies the test with $H^i(R\Gamma(T,E))$. These groups vanish above some $b$. The affine derived equivalence reconstructs $E$ from $M=R\Gamma(T,E)$ by termwise tilde, and the existing tilde-homology comparison gives $\mathcal H^i(E)\cong\widetilde{H^i(M)}=0$ for $i>b$. The empty affine also satisfies this argument.

source.place: Tag 0GEN, affine base case; 06Z0, lemma-affine-compare-bounded; coherent.tex 08DR

proof.text: For the induction step write $T=U\cup V$, with $U$ quasi-compact open, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine, and assume $\mathscr P(U)$, $\mathscr P(V)$ and $\mathscr P(U\cap V)$. Let $E$ satisfy the all-perfect-Hom condition on $T$ and put $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $v:V\hookrightarrow T$. A finite affine cover of $U$, together with quasi-compactness of intersections of affine opens in the quasi-separated scheme $T$, shows $W=U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. Write the closed subset $V\setminus W=V(I)$ for an ideal $I\subset A$. The principal opens $D(f)$ with $f\in I$ cover $W$ by the definition of the Zariski topology; quasi-compactness selects $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ with $W=\bigcup D(f_k)$. Let $C$ be their cochain Koszul object. The affine Koszul properties make $C$ perfect with cohomology supported on $Z=T\setminus U$, which is closed in $T$ and contained in $V$.

source.place: Tag 0GEN, gluing step, choice of f_1,...,f_r and the supported Koszul object

proof.text:
Apply the supported open-pushforward theorem to $v$ and $C$. It gives a perfect object $C'=Rv_*C$ on $T$ and identifies it with $v_!C$. The open-extension adjunction consequently identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C[-i],E|_V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!C[-i],E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C'[-i],E).$$
By the hypothesis on $E$, choose $a$ so that these groups vanish for every $i\geq a$. The affine Koszul upper-localization lemma, applied on $V$ to $E|_V$ and $W\hookrightarrow V$, now gives the isomorphism
$$\tau_{\geq a}(E|_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\geq a}R(W\hookrightarrow V)_*(E|_W).$$

source.place: Tag 0GEN, equation 0GEP and subsequent use of 0GEJ; cohomology.tex 08DP, 08DF, 08BS

proof.text: Set $F=Rj_*(E|_U)$ and let $u:E\to F$ be the actual restriction-adjunction unit. On $U$ its restriction is an isomorphism, by the derived open-unit restriction theorem. On $V$, the open restriction/direct-image comparison identifies this unit with the unit used in step 4: both are induced by restriction of a K-injective representative, so their maps on sections agree. Hence $\mathcal H^n(u)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\geq a$, since it is so on the cover $U,V$. Complete $u$ to a triangle $E\to F\to B\to E[1]$. Its cohomology sequence gives $\mathcal H^n(B)=0$ for $n\geq a$. The open immersion $j$ is qcqs by qcqs-morphism permanence, so $F$ has quasi-coherent cohomology; Apply the supported quasi-coherent triangulated-property theorem with support equal to all of $T$. Its shift stability and middle-term closure, applied to the rotated triangle $F\to B\to E[1]\to F[1]$, give $B\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$.

source.place: Tag 0GEN, canonical upper-truncation isomorphism on the two opens; cohomology.tex 08FE; perfect.tex 08D5

proof.text:
Fix a perfect $Q$ on $T$. By perfect-gap vanishing there is a finite interval $[c,d]$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,L)=0$ whenever the quasi-coherent $L$ has zero cohomology in that interval. Since $B\in D^{\leq a-1}$, we have $\mathcal H^q(B[i])=\mathcal H^{q+i}(B)=0$ for $q\in[c,d]$ as soon as $i>a-1-c$; the same holds for $B[i-1]$ as soon as $i>a-c$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],B)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],B[-1])$ are zero for large $i$. Apply Hom exactness to the triangle of step 5 and its rotations. The segment
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],B[-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],E)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],F)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],B)$$
shows that $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],F)=0$ for $i\gg0$. This writes out the two bounded-truncation comparisons used in Stacks 0GEL; no new bound uniform in $Q$ has been asserted.

Let $P$ be any perfect object on $U$. Apply the perfect-support map-lifting lemma with ambient scheme $T$, closed support equal to all of $T$, target object zero, and map $P\to0|_U$ equal to zero. Its support hypotheses are automatic and $T\setminus T=\varnothing$ is quasi-compact. It supplies a perfect $Q$ on $T$ and maps $P\to Q|_U\to P$ with composite $1_P$. For an open immersion, the module pullback/restriction comparison identifies $j^*$ with exact restriction. Applying the K-flat formula for derived pullback to a resolution, exactness of restriction identifies $Lj^*Q$ with $Q|_U$. Derived pullback/direct-image adjunction therefore identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q[-i],F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}((Q|_U)[-i],E|_U).$$
Step 6 makes this group zero eventually. Precomposition with the displayed splitting makes $\operatorname{Hom}(P[-i],E|_U)$ a retract of it, hence zero eventually. Since this holds for every $P$, the induction hypothesis $\mathscr P(U)$ gives an integer $b$ with $\mathcal H^n(E|_U)=0$ for $n>b$. This uses all perfect tests on $U$, so no additional single-generator detection theorem is needed.

Apply the uniform derived direct-image bound to $j:U\to T$ and $(E|_U)[b]$, whose positive cohomology vanishes. The target $T$ is quasi-compact, and $j$ is qcqs as checked in step 5. For its integer $N>0$ we obtain $\mathcal H^m(F[b])=0$ for $m\geq N$, hence $\mathcal H^n(F)=0$ for $n\geq b+N$. For every $n\geq\max(a,b+N)$, step 5 identifies $\mathcal H^n(E)$ with this zero sheaf. This proves $\mathscr P(T)$ and completes the gluing implication. The induction principle in step 2 gives $\mathscr P(X)$; applying it to the Hom tests of step 1 proves the stated bound for $K$. Every bound chosen was for an individual perfect object or an individual cover step, as permitted by the hypothesis.
